Subject: ACME POC — Evaluation plan & success criteria

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the plan captured: 

Summary of goals (from today):
- Validate Redwood's relevance and factuality on Acme's product support dialogs (priority use case).
- Ensure latency and cost are within Acme thresholds for the pilot.
- Confirm integration & data handling for customer PII and auditability.

Draft success criteria (attached: POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx):
1) Relevance: 85%+ pass rate on our rubric for top-10 support intents (scored by offline eval).
2) Factuality: <5% hallucination rate on sampled tickets (manual review + automated checks).
3) Latency: 95th percentile < 400ms for sampled production traffic during shadowing.
4) Cost: token cost per session <= your target (we'll confirm exact number from your finance).
5) Ops readiness: logging, audit trails, and key rotation validated during the run.

Evaluation approach (high-level):
- Offline evals: run seeded test set + edge-case prompts (repeatable, fast iterations).
- Online shadow: run live traffic sample (no customer-facing changes) to validate behavior in the wild and measure latency/cost.
- Grading rubric: initial draft attached (eval_rubric.pdf) — categories: relevance, factuality, safety, latency, cost.

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 0 (setup): Redwood infra + eval harness + dataset ingestion (2 weeks to baseline).
- Weeks 2–6: Eval window (offline and rolling online shadow).
- Week 7: Final review, remediation, and decision.

Action items / asks from Acme:
- Confirm owners for data access and POC acceptance (who on your side will provide training/test data and own acceptance?).
- Confirm any additional success metrics not listed above.
- Sign off on timeline or propose adjustments.

Attachments: POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx (draft), eval_rubric.pdf (draft).

Thanks — I can iterate the docs once you confirm the owners and any metric tweaks. Planning to loop Marissa on the rubric and eval harness setup.

—

Subject: Re: ACME POC — Evaluation plan & success criteria — rubric & methodology notes

Hi all — tagging in some concrete methodology notes to align expectations for offline vs online and the grading rubric. High level notes below; happy to run a 30–45 min rubric walkthrough after you review.

Offline evaluations (what we'll run):
- Dataset: snapshot of historical support tickets + synthetic edge-case prompts. ACME to provide labeled set for the 12 intents (we'll use as seed).
- Metrics: precision/recall per intent, weighted relevance score, factuality flag rate. We'll run batch scoring and produce per-case annotations.
- Annotation: create a small manual labeling batch (200 cases) to measure IAA; use that to adjust thresholds.

Online shadow (production sampling):
- Sampling: start at 1% of traffic for non-critical routes, hold out any flows that include PII or financial transactions until explicit approval.
- Safety: run safety filters + fallback policy in shadow path; no user-facing responses changed.
- Observability: log prompt/response, latency, token counts, safety flags, and upstream event ids for traceability.

Grading rubric (proposed categories & thresholds):
- Relevance (weight 40%): pass if weighted relevance >= 0.88 across sampled set.
- Factuality (weight 30%): major hallucinations <= 2% in critical intents; minor <= 5% overall.
- Safety (weight 10%): zero high-severity safety violations in sample.
- Latency (weight 10%): p95 < 400ms, p99 < 800ms for critical endpoints.
- Cost (weight 10%): token cost delta within agreed threshold.

Notes on automation: we'll provide scripts for automated scoring, export a per-case CSV, and generate a dashboard for per-intent slices. For manual review we'll use the same UI your labeling team uses so there's minimal context switching.

Open questions / asks:
- ACME: can we get a labeled sample of 1,000 cases for the top 12 intents by 2026-11-26? (this helps seed the offline baseline)
- Which endpoints are considered "critical" for p99 tracking?

If that works I'll schedule a rubric walkthrough and post the invite.

Best,
